items.q: Which method returns a single SelenideElement by CSS selector?
items.e: $() is the primary method for finding a single element by CSS or XPath.

items.q: Which method returns a collection of elements?
items.e: $$() returns an ElementsCollection — a collection of all matching elements.

items.q: Which condition checks that an element is visible?
items.e: Condition.visible — the element is in the DOM and visible. exist/present only check DOM presence.

items.q: How do you open a URL in Selenide?
items.e: The static open(url) method is the standard way to navigate in Selenide.

items.q: Which method uploads a file via input type file?
items.e: uploadFile(new File(path)) correctly uploads a file even for hidden input elements.

items.q: What does shouldBe() do?
o: Checks a condition with waiting and throws AssertionError
items.e: shouldBe() is an assertion with built-in waiting until timeout; it throws AssertionError on failure.

items.q: What is the default timeout in Selenide?
items.e: By default Selenide waits 4 seconds. Change it via Configuration.timeout.

items.q: How do you change the global timeout?
items.e: Configuration.timeout = N sets the timeout in milliseconds for all Selenide waits.

items.q: Which condition checks that an element is in the DOM (even hidden)?
items.e: Condition.exist (or Condition.present) — the element is in the DOM regardless of visibility.

items.q: How do you check that an element is NOT visible?
items.e: Both are correct: shouldBe(hidden) and shouldNotBe(visible) are equivalent.

items.q: How do you click an element in Selenide?
items.e: $(sel).click() — a direct method call on the SelenideElement.

items.q: How do you type text into an input, clearing the previous content?
items.e: setValue() clears the field and types the new text. sendKeys() appends to the existing content.

items.q: How do you get an element's text?
items.e: $(sel).text() returns the element's visible text content.

items.q: How do you assert an element's text?
items.e: shouldHave(Condition.text()) — a text assertion with waiting. text() checks substring containment.

items.q: What does Condition.exactText() check?
items.e: exactText() checks the full text match, unlike text() which looks for a substring.

items.q: How do you check the href attribute value?
items.e: shouldHave(Condition.attribute(name, value)) — an attribute assertion with waiting.

items.q: Which condition checks an element's CSS class?
items.e: Condition.cssClass("name") checks that the element has the given CSS class.

items.q: How do you check that a checkbox is checked?
items.e: Both Condition.selected and Condition.checked verify checkbox/radio state.

items.q: How do you get an attribute value?
items.e: Both attr() and getAttribute() return the attribute value.

items.q: How do you get a CSS property value?
items.e: getCssValue() and css() — both methods return the CSS property value.

items.q: How do you select an option in a select by text?
items.e: selectOption("text") is Selenide's convenient method for selecting by visible text.

items.q: How do you select an option in a select by value?
items.e: selectOptionByValue() or setValue() — both work for selecting by the value attribute.

items.q: How do you hover over an element?
items.e: $(sel).hover() is Selenide's built-in mouse-over method, no Actions API needed.

items.q: How do you perform a double-click?
items.e: $(sel).dblclick() is the double-click method in Selenide.

items.q: How do you perform a right-click?
items.e: $(sel).contextClick() opens the context menu (right click).

items.q: How do you press the Enter key on an element?
items.e: Both are correct: sendKeys(Keys.ENTER) and pressEnter().

items.q: How do you clear an input field?
items.e: clear() and setValue("") both clear the field. clear() is a Selenium method, setValue("") is Selenide.

items.q: What does $$(sel).first() mean?
o: The first element of the collection
items.e: first() returns the first SelenideElement of the collection, same as get(0).

items.q: What does $$(sel).last() mean?
o: The last element of the collection
The element with the highest z-index
items.e: last() returns the last element of the collection.

items.q: How do you get an element by index in a collection?
items.e: $$(sel).get(i) — access by (zero-based) index.

items.q: How do you assert the number of elements in a collection?
items.e: CollectionCondition.size(n) — a collection size assertion with waiting.

items.q: Which condition checks that a collection is not empty?
items.e: notEmpty() and sizeGreaterThan(0) — both check the collection has at least one element.

items.q: How do you switch to an iframe?
items.e: $(sel).switchTo() switches context to the iframe represented by the element.

items.q: How do you return from an iframe to the main content?
items.e: switchTo().defaultContent() — the standard WebDriver method, available via Selenide.switchTo().

items.q: How do you switch to a new window/tab?
items.e: switchTo().window(title) switches to a window by its title or handle.

items.q: Which method takes a screenshot in Selenide?
items.e: Selenide.screenshot("name") saves a screenshot and returns the file path.

items.q: Where does Selenide store screenshots by default?
items.e: By default screenshots go to target/screenshots (Maven project).

items.q: How do you configure the screenshots folder?
items.e: Configuration.reportsFolder sets the folder for screenshots and other reports.

items.q: What is SelenideElement?
o: A wrapper around WebElement with lazy init and assertions
items.e: SelenideElement wraps WebElement with lazy initialization, auto-waiting and convenient assertions.

items.q: What is Configuration.browser for?
items.e: Configuration.browser = "chrome"/"firefox"/"edge" — selects the browser for tests.

items.q: How do you enable headless mode?
items.e: Configuration.headless = true is the simplest way to enable headless mode in Selenide.

items.q: What does Selenide.closeWebDriver() do?
o: Closes the WebDriver and the browser
items.e: closeWebDriver() shuts down the WebDriver and all browser windows. Usually called in @AfterAll.

items.q: How does Selenide handle StaleElementReferenceException?
items.e: Selenide handles StaleElementReferenceException automatically by re-locating the element.

items.q: What are soft assertions in Selenide?
o: Assertions that don't stop the test on failure
items.e: Soft assertions collect all failures and report them together at the end without stopping the test.

items.q: How do you enable soft assertions in JUnit5?
items.e: @ExtendWith(SoftAssertionsExtension.class) — the JUnit5 extension for automatic soft assertions.

items.q: What is Condition.matchText()?
items.e: Condition.matchText(regex) checks the element text against a regular expression.

items.q: Which method executes JavaScript in Selenide?
items.e: Selenide.executeScript() wraps JavascriptExecutor.executeScript().

items.q: How do you check an input's value attribute?
items.e: Condition.value() and attribute("value") — both check the value attribute.

items.q: How do you find a child element inside a parent?
items.e: $(parent).$(child) and $(parent).find(child) — both search nested elements.

items.q: How do you find all child elements?
items.e: $$(child) and findAll(child) on a SelenideElement find all matching descendants.

items.q: What is ElementsCollection.filterBy()?
o: Filters the collection by a condition
items.e: filterBy(condition) returns a new collection with only the elements matching the condition.

items.q: What does $$(sel).excludeWith(condition) do?
o: Returns the collection without elements matching the condition
items.e: excludeWith(condition) is the opposite of filterBy — it excludes matching elements.

items.q: Which condition checks that a field is disabled?
items.e: Condition.disabled checks that the element has the disabled attribute.

items.q: Which condition checks that a field is enabled?
items.e: Condition.enabled checks the element is active and available for interaction.

items.q: How do you check that an element is focused?
items.e: shouldBe(Condition.focused) checks the element currently has focus.

items.q: How do you download a file in Selenide?
items.e: $(sel).download() downloads the file and returns a File object.

items.q: What is Configuration.fileDownload?
o: The file download strategy (HTTPGET, FOLDER, CDP)
items.e: Configuration.fileDownload sets the download strategy: HTTPGET, FOLDER or CDP.

items.q: What is Configuration.proxyEnabled?
o: Enables Selenide's built-in proxy for intercepting requests
items.e: proxyEnabled = true turns on the built-in BrowserMob proxy for intercepting traffic and downloads.

items.q: How do you assert the page URL?
items.e: webdriver().shouldHave(urlContaining()) or urlStartingWith() — URL assertions with waiting.

items.q: How do you assert the page title?
items.e: webdriver().shouldHave(title("text")) — the page title assertion.

items.q: What is Selenide.refresh()?
items.e: Selenide.refresh() reloads the current page (like F5).

items.q: Which method navigates back to the previous page?
items.e: Selenide.back() — the convenient static back-navigation method.

items.q: What does $(sel).scrollTo() do?
o: Scrolls the page to the element
items.e: $(sel).scrollTo() scrolls the viewport so the element becomes visible.

items.q: How do you scroll to an element via JS?
items.e: $(sel).scrollIntoView(true) runs JavaScript scrollIntoView for precise positioning.

items.q: What is $x() in Selenide?
items.e: $x("//xpath") is a shorthand for $(By.xpath("//xpath")).

items.q: How do you find an element by link text?
items.e: By.linkText() for an exact match and By.partialLinkText() for a partial one — both work in Selenide.

items.q: How do you access the underlying WebDriver from Selenide?
items.e: WebDriverRunner.getWebDriver() returns the current WebDriver instance.

items.q: What is WebDriverRunner.setWebDriver()?
o: Sets an external WebDriver as the current one
items.e: setWebDriver() lets you pass your own WebDriver instance when Selenide shouldn't create it.

items.q: How do you set Chrome options in Selenide?
items.e: Create ChromeOptions and pass it into Configuration.browserCapabilities.

items.q: What is @Rule SelenideRule (JUnit4)?
o: Takes a screenshot on test failure
items.e: SelenideRule automatically takes a screenshot when a JUnit4 test fails.

items.q: What is the difference between shouldBe() and shouldHave()?
o: shouldBe for states, shouldHave for properties — semantically
items.e: shouldBe() and shouldHave() are aliases, functionally identical. The difference is purely semantic.

items.q: What is Condition.and()?
o: A logical OR of two conditions
A logical AND of two conditions
A condition with a custom timeout
items.e: Condition.and("name", cond1, cond2) — checks that both conditions hold at the same time.

items.q: What is Condition.or()?
o: A logical OR — at least one condition holds
items.e: Condition.or("name", cond1, cond2) — passes if at least one of the conditions is true.

items.q: How do you check that an element does NOT exist in the DOM?
items.e: shouldNotBe(exist) and shouldBe(missing) — both verify the element is absent from the DOM.

items.q: How do you send several keys at once (Ctrl+A)?
items.e: Keys.chord() combines keys into a single string for sendKeys.

items.q: What is ElementsCollection.texts()?
o: Returns a List<String> with all elements' texts
items.e: texts() returns a list of strings with the texts of all collection elements.

items.q: Which collection condition checks for specific texts?
items.e: texts() — containment, exactTexts() — exact match. Both check all elements of the collection.

items.q: What is SelenideAppiumDriver?
o: A driver for mobile testing via Appium
items.e: SelenideAppiumDriver integrates Selenide with Appium for mobile testing.

items.q: How do you configure a Remote WebDriver (Selenium Grid)?
items.e: Configuration.remote = "http://grid-url/wd/hub" — remote driver setup.

items.q: What is Configuration.browserSize?
o: The browser window size in "WxH" format
items.e: Configuration.browserSize = "1920x1080" sets the browser window size.

items.q: How do you use a custom WebDriverProvider?
o: Implement WebDriverFactory and pass it to Configuration.browserCapabilities
Implement WebDriverProvider and pass the class to Configuration.browser
items.e: Configuration.browser = MyWebDriverProvider.class.getName() — a custom driver provider.

items.q: What is Selenide.confirm()?
items.e: Selenide.confirm() presses OK on a JavaScript alert/confirm dialog.

items.q: What is Selenide.dismiss()?
items.e: Selenide.dismiss() presses Cancel on a JavaScript confirm dialog.

items.q: How do you get the text of a JavaScript alert?
items.e: switchTo().alert().getText() — the standard WebDriver way to read the alert text.

items.q: What is Condition.href()?
o: Checks that href contains a substring
items.e: Condition.href(url) checks the exact value of the element's href attribute.

items.q: How do you check a field's placeholder?
items.e: Both options are valid for checking the placeholder.

items.q: What is $(sel).as("name")?
items.e: as("name") gives the element a readable name shown in logs and error messages.

items.q: How do you set a custom assertion error message?
items.e: $(sel).as("msg").shouldBe(visible) is the cleanest way to add error context.

items.q: What is Selenide.sleep()?
items.e: Selenide.sleep(ms) wraps Thread.sleep(). Use it only as a last resort.

items.q: Which JUnit5 annotation closes the browser after all tests?
items.e: @AfterAll static void tearDown() { closeWebDriver(); } — closes the browser after the whole class.

items.q: What is Configuration.holdBrowserOpen?
o: Keeps the browser open after tests (for debugging)
items.e: holdBrowserOpen = true leaves the browser open after the tests for debugging.

items.q: How do you check a radio button's state?
items.e: checked, selected and attribute("checked") — all three work for radio/checkbox state.

items.q: What is $$(sel).shouldHave(CollectionCondition.itemWithText("text"))?
o: Checks that at least one element contains the text
items.e: itemWithText("text") checks the collection has at least one element with the given text.

items.q: How does Selenide integrate with Allure?
items.e: Add the selenide-allure dependency and @ExtendWith(AllureSelenide.class) for automatic screenshots in Allure.

items.q: What is the AllureSelenide listener?
o: Attaches screenshots and logs to the Allure report
items.e: AllureSelenide automatically attaches step screenshots and failure details to the Allure report.

items.q: What is Configuration.screenshots?
items.e: Configuration.screenshots = true/false — toggles automatic screenshots on test failure.

items.q: What is Configuration.savePageSource?
o: Saves the page HTML on failure
items.e: savePageSource = true saves the page HTML next to the screenshot on failure.

items.q: Which Maven artifact brings in Selenide?
items.e: com.codeborne:selenide:VERSION — the official Maven artifact from the Selenide author.

items.q: What is $(sel).shouldBe(visible, Duration.ofSeconds(10))?
o: Sets a custom timeout for this assertion only
items.e: Duration.ofSeconds(10) as the second shouldBe() argument sets the timeout for this specific wait only.

items.q: Which method clicks a button that is outside the viewport?
items.e: scrollTo().click() first scrolls to the element, then clicks it.

items.q: What is $(sel).parent()?
items.e: $(sel).parent() returns the SelenideElement that is the immediate parent node.

items.q: How do you find the closest ancestor by CSS?
items.e: $(sel).closest("css") — like jQuery's closest(), finds the nearest ancestor matching the selector.

items.q: What is $(sel).sibling(n)?
o: An element at the same level by index
items.e: sibling(n) returns the n-th following sibling of the current element.

items.q: What is $(sel).preceding(n)?
items.e: preceding(n) returns the n-th preceding sibling.

items.q: What is Condition.interactable?
o: The element is visible and enabled
The element is in the viewport
The element is not covered by another
The element is visible + enabled + not covered
items.e: Condition.interactable checks the element is visible, enabled and not overlapped by another element.

items.q: Which method performs drag and drop in Selenide?
items.e: $(sel).dragAndDropTo(SelenideElement target) or dragAndDropTo(String cssSelector).

items.q: What is Configuration.pollingInterval?
o: How often conditions are polled while waiting
items.e: pollingInterval — how often (in ms) a condition is re-checked while waiting. Default is 200 ms.
